chapter: Billy Pierce Studio and New York tap
title: Cotton Club boys, Bardu Ali and Broadway producers at the studio
summary: Green names others who frequented the studio, including Bardu Ali, Cagney, Earl Carroll and George White, as a place to find talent.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well, I was saying about Billy Pierce studio. You see, these fellows -- he became a teacher. That's Buster Newman, see, and then there was these Cotton Club boys like Louis Brown and Stretch Johnson, and even the band leader used to come there, this Bardu Ali (PHONETIC), he and his brother had an act. They used to come there.
Who eventually became Red Foxx's manager.
Yeah. He became Red Foxx's manager. He used to have a lot of laughs with us, you know. Because of the eyes, you see.
I think it became the in place for looking for talent, as you said, George.

Yeah. Well, it had to be. George M. Cohan was coming there, I mean, really. See, and a lot of these people were interested in like James Cagney -- see, he was in the process of being discovered by the moving pictures, you see. Earl Carroll, he used to come in there. George White. See, it was very important people in theater.
Broadway was getting into its peak.
